title: Tickner and Ferguson Ruled Out as New Zealand Reshuffle Again for India ODIs
excerpt: Blair Tickner must serve a seven-day stand-down despite being cleared of concussion, Lockie Ferguson is out for the series with a calf tear, and Kristian Clarke comes in as cover with India leading 2-0 before Tuesday's Hamilton match.
body:
• Blair Tickner will miss New Zealand's next two ODIs against India after being struck while batting in Wellington — cleared of concussion, but required to serve the ICC's mandatory seven-day stand-down after being replaced by Matt Fisher.
  • Lockie Ferguson is ruled out of the rest of the series with a low-grade right-calf tear sustained during the T20I series.
  • Kristian Clarke has been added as bowling cover; Matt Henry will miss Tuesday's third ODI in Hamilton and is targeting the fourth ODI.
  • India lead the five-match series 2-0, so New Zealand must win in Hamilton to keep the series alive.

New Zealand have made further changes to their squad for the remaining matches of the five-match ODI series against India, with fast bowlers Blair Tickner and Lockie Ferguson ruled out and Matt Henry set to miss the third match, New Zealand Cricket said on Monday, November 9.

Tickner: cleared, but stood down

Tickner was struck by a ball while batting during the second ODI in Wellington. He has since been cleared of concussion, but because he was replaced in the playing XI by Matt Fisher, he is required to follow the ICC's mandatory seven-day stand-down from the date of the match before returning to international cricket, the NZC release said, according to ANI. Northern Districts fast bowler Kristian Clarke comes into the squad as cover.

Ferguson out, Henry delayed

Ferguson has been ruled out of the fourth and fifth ODIs because he has not fully recovered from the low-grade right-calf tear sustained during the T20I series. Henry, initially cleared of concussion after his training collision with Devon Conway in Auckland and reassessed in Wellington, will miss Tuesday's third ODI in Hamilton and is aiming to return for the fourth ODI, NZC said. Henry and Kyle Jamieson, who were initially heading to the Test camp in Wellington after the third ODI, will now remain with the ODI squad for the fourth match as well, according to IANS.

A squad split by the Test series

The reshuffle is compounded by the calendar. Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips and Nathan Smith will leave Hamilton on Wednesday to begin preparations for the World Test Championship series against India and will be unavailable for the final ODI; two players are set to be added across the fourth and fifth matches, and the squad for the fifth ODI has not yet been announced. New Zealand are already without Conway, ruled out with concussion, and Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman, who remain unavailable with shoulder and hamstring injuries.

The named squads underline the churn. For the third ODI: Mitchell Santner (captain), Michael Bracewell, Kristian Clarke, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Kyle Jamieson, Nick Kelly, Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips, Tim Seifert, Nathan Smith and Will Young. For the fourth ODI: Santner, Finn Allen, Bracewell, Clarke, Duffy, Fisher, Dean Foxcroft, Mitch Hay, Matt Henry, Jamieson, Kelly, Seifert and Young. With India 2-0 up, Tuesday's match in Hamilton is a must-win for the hosts.
